Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Solara Renewables Inc. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. If you would like to ask a question at that time, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. We ask that you limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Solara Renewables Inc.'s results for the Q2 2024. Joining me on today's call are Mark Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Mike Harlan, Chief Financial Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Development Officer; and Emma Patel, Chief Sustainability Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Mark Thompson.

Mark Thompson:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Solara Renewables had a strong Q2, reflecting our commitment to innovation and sustainability in the renewable energy sector. We continue to see increasing demand for our clean energy solutions and are well-positioned to capitalize on the growing market opportunities.

We want to highlight five crucial aspects of this quarter's achievements:

1. Our development pipeline additions and project milestones.
2. Revenue and earnings growth analysis.
3. Debt levels and financing costs.
4. PPA pricing trends and contract extensions.
5. Strategic priorities and outlook for the next quarter and year.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Harlan to provide a detailed overview of our financial performance.

Mike Harlan:
Thank you, Mark. We are pleased with our financial results for the Q2 2024. Good morning, everyone, and thanks for being on Solara Renewables' second quarter earnings call. As a leader in integrated solar PV, wind, and energy storage solutions—with more than 15 GW of projects developed globally since our 2021 IPO—we've executed exceptionally well, supported by the U.S. Inflation Reduction Act, Europe's REPowerEU plan, and surging corporate PPAs against elevated energy prices.

Starting with the top-line figures that highlight our growth path: Q2 revenue hit $452 million, up 35% year-over-year from $335 million in Q2 2023 and 12% sequentially from $403 million in Q1 2024. This is our eighth consecutive quarter of double-digit YoY revenue gains. Adjusted EBITDA reached $128 million, a 42% YoY jump, delivering a solid 28.3% margin—better by 180 basis points thanks to operating scale and better module costs.

Net income to Solara shareholders came in at $76 million, or $0.87 per diluted share, beating consensus by $0.09 and up 93% from $39 million or $0.45 EPS last year. Our trailing 12-month ROIC is now 14.2%, comfortably above our cost of capital, thanks to our asset-light focus on development, EPC, and ongoing O&M services.

Growth spanned all segments, powered by 3.2 GW of new project awards—our best in two years. Solar PV, 52% of revenue at $235 million, surged 48% YoY on bifacial TOPCon modules and a fresh 1 GW U.S. utility pipeline tapping IRA Section 45X credits. ASPs stayed at $0.28 per watt DC amid global supply, secured by offtake with NextEra and Duke Energy. Standout: the 500 MW Desert Sun project in Arizona with a $28 per MWh LCOE, outcompeting local gas peakers.

Onshore wind, 28% of revenue or $127 million, rose 22% YoY via turbine sales and EPC for ten 5 MW Siemens Gamesa units. Margins hit 26% through our Texas nacelle assembly, protecting against Red Sea issues. Key: a 300 MW PPA with Google for our Oklahoma site at $35 per MWh over 15 years.

Energy storage, 15% of revenue at $68 million, skyrocketed 65% YoY amid CAISO and ERCOT curtailments. We rolled out 1.2 GWh of LFP packs via CATL partnership, including a 400 MWh four-hour setup paired with solar in California. This yielded 32% gross margins boosted by up to 10% IRA domestic content adders.

EPC and O&M services rounded out at 5% or $22 million, up 15% YoY with recurring revenue from a 5 GW backlog. Utilization climbed to 92% from 87% prior year.

By region, North America fueled 60% of the growth at 45% YoY, energized by $4.5 billion in IRA ITC/PTC transfer deals this quarter—following Enphase and First Solar strategies. U.S. backlog stands at 8.5 GW, 70% from Texas and California.

Europe, 25% of revenue, advanced 28% YoY toward REPowerEU's 320 GW solar/wind by 2030 targets. Wins: 200 MW floating solar in the Netherlands with our HDPE floater tech, plus UK CfD auctions at £40 per MWh.

APAC and emerging markets at 15% grew 20%, offset by China's module surplus but lifted by India's 50 GW tenders. We're scaling a 500 MW Rajasthan project with Adani Green, leveraging perovskite tandem R&D for over 25% efficiencies.

This growth is structural, with global clean energy capex at $550 billion in 2023 per BNEF and storage growing at 45% CAGR to 2030. Our 12 GW development pipeline—up 20% quarter-over-quarter—and $2.8 billion contracted backlog give 2.5 times visibility into our raised full-year revenue guide of $1.95 billion, up 32% YoY from $1.90 billion prior.

Margin expansion stemmed from 29.5% gross margins overall, up 250 basis points on higher fixed-cost leverage and savings from our 5 GW module inventory; SG&A at 12% of revenue via AI-optimized asset management cutting O&M 15%; and tax efficiency at 22% effective rate including IRA elective pay.

Headwinds like 10% quarter-over-quarter polysilicon drops are countered by hedging and U.S. manufacturing ramps. On rates, our $1.2 billion green bond at 4.2% fixed ensures DSCR over 2.0 times.

For FY 2024, we guide revenue to $1.95 to $2.05 billion—midpoint 32% YoY growth—adjusted EBITDA $520 to $560 million at 28% margins, and EPS $3.40 to $3.60. Q3 revenue around $510 million. Long-term, 20-25% CAGR to 2027, with green hydrogen pilots like our 50 MW electrolyzer JV with Plug Power entering high-margin territory by 2026.

Shifting to our balance sheet strength and debt profile, a key focus amid macro shifts and cleantech's capital intensity. At June 30, total gross debt was $5.2 billion: $3.8 billion in long-term project finance for our 12 GW portfolio of utility-scale solar, onshore wind, and BESS, plus $1.4 billion corporate revolver and term loans. Netting $1.1 billion unrestricted cash from strong free cash flow off stabilized Southwest solar assets, net debt is $4.1 billion. That's a net debt-to-adjusted EBITDA of 3.2 times, improved from 3.8 times year-end 2023 and inside our 2.5 to 3.5 times target—better than NextEra Energy Partners' roughly 4.0 times, despite adding 1.2 GW commissioned year-to-date.

Project debt, 73% of total and non-recourse against PPAs with investment-grade buyers like Google and PG&E, shows average trailing 12-month DSCRs of 1.8 times, above the 1.5 times sector norm. Corporate side: upsized $1.5 billion revolver led by JPMorgan and BofA, with $800 million undrawn for liquidity.

Financing costs averaged an all-in 4.2% interest rate this quarter, up just 20 basis points year-over-year from lagged Fed hikes on our 25% floating exposure, which we've hedged heavily. Q2 interest expense was $178 million, up 12% YoY but only 8.5% of adjusted EBITDA versus industry 10-12% for growth names like Orsted or Vestas.

Key moves: In April, a $750 million green bond at 3.75% coupon—our tightest—under ICMA principles, funding 500 MW California BESS expansion and capturing a 50 basis point greenium amid EU Green Deal and IRA flows.

Our hedging covers 85% of floating project debt fixed to 2027 via SOFR caps and collars at 4.25% average strike, dodging recent 50 basis point SOFR jumps and saving $25 million annually versus peers.

Tax equity monetized $400 million via partnerships with Clearway Energy, using IRA 30-50% ITCs to blend equity into funding and drop WACC to 5.8% from pre-IRA 6.5% on new projects.

U.S. debt (65%) enjoys inflation-linked IRA PPAs with 60-65% LTVs on Texas/Arizona solar. Europe (25%) for North Sea wind akin to Orsted's Hornsea uses €500 million KfW loans under 3%. APAC (10%) taps yen Samurai bonds hedging AUD for 300 MW Australia.

Forward priorities: Refinance $1 billion legacy over-5% debt to sub-4% greens, saving $40 million yearly; growth deleveraging from 2.5 GW construction yielding $600 million revolver inflows for 0.5 times leverage drop by year-end; covenant buffers of 25% on interest coverage and 20% on leverage, passing +200 basis point stress tests.

Full-year interest $720-750 million at 4.1-4.3% effective, net debt/EBITDA to 3.0 times by Q4. Mitigants like 92% fixed-price backlog and diverse offtake counter inflation or emerging PPA risks. This setup fuels 20% CAGR while eyeing AI datacenter-driven BESS IRRs of 12-15%.

Before moving on, a quick note on PPA pricing trends and extensions, central to our revenue stability for the 12 GW operating assets and 18 GW pipeline across solar, wind, and BESS. LevelTen's latest U.S. solar PPA index shows $26 per MWh average in Q3—up 3% YoY but down 2% sequentially—stabilizing after 2018-2021 drops to $20 per MWh unsubsidized in sunny Southwest spots. National wind holds at $28 per MWh, supported by high-capacity-factor newer turbines like Vestas V150-15.0 MW in our Texas Panhandle builds.

Inflation in polysilicon and balance-of-system has slowed declines, but tech keeps LCOEs sharp: NREL at $24-36 per MWh solar and $26-43 wind unsubsidized, under $50-60 per MWh ERCOT merchant summer peaks. In Europe JV with Orsted North Sea, UK solar at £35 per MWh ($44) down 8% YoY post-subsidy shifts; German EEG auctions cleared €0.042 per kWh ($46 per MWh) for 4.5 GW PV.

U.S. Southwest/ERCOT leads: CAISO 300 MW solar-plus-storage with SCE at $28 per MWh for 20 years, plus $5 per MWh resource adequacy from four-hour BESS. ERCOT volatility—$100 per MWh daytime solar LMPs August—enables $32 per MWh blends on fixed PPAs with merchant collars for Pecos Solar 450 MW expansion. PJM softer at $24 per MWh due to queues; we're investing $200 million in substations for exits.

Extensions de-risked 1.2 GW or 15% of operating fleet: 10-year renewal on 400 MW Desert Sun Arizona wind at 12% premium to original $22 per MWh with 2% CPI escalator. California Valley 250 MW solar with PG&E at $30 per MWh, up 18%, via TOPCon repower (22.5% efficiency) and trackers lifting yield 15-20%.

Bundling BESS with IRA 30% ITC qualifies firming deals: MISO 200 MW/800 MWh with frequency regulation adding $8 per MWh ancillaries. 85% success rate using our Aurora tool's 98% load-shape match for Google/Microsoft.

Our 95% contracted 24 GW backlog to 2045 sets us up strong. FY24 blended PPA pricing up 4-6% to $29 per MWh, with 80% uncontracted hedged at $35 floors via Goldman financial PPAs. Mitigants: 2.5 GW First Solar offtake against TOPCon wafers; rate sensitivity trimmed as every 50 basis point Fed rise cuts IRRs 20-30 basis points.

We're evolving to PPA 2.0: 25+ year tenors, ESG escalators via Verra carbon verification, H2 hybrids. Australia 500 MW Sun Cable extension with AGL at AUD 55 per MWh integrates 50 MW electrolyzer under $15 per kg incentives.

Overall, pricing at LCOE parity with double-digit extension premiums supports raised FY guidance of $1.8-2.0 billion contracted revenue and 18-20% EBITDA margins.

Our financial outlook remains bright, with operating expenses at around $210 million driven by R&D and market expansion, maintaining our strong balance sheet.

Now, I'll pass the call to Jordan to discuss our project development pipeline.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Mike. Our project development pipeline continues to grow, with 28.7 GW of projects under development across various renewable energy technologies. Good morning, everyone—in the renewables space, a strong, de-risked pipeline fuels enduring growth, especially with Inflation Reduction Act tailwinds like uncapped PTC/ITC transferability driving 8-10% YoY LCOE drops for utility solar and wind per Lazard's recent data.

Headline for Q2: We added a record 4.2 GW globally, lifting total owned/controlled capacity to 28.7 GW in solar PV, onshore wind, BESS, and nascent green hydrogen. That's 17% quarter-over-quarter growth, placing us top-quartile among pure-play developers with 85% pipeline-to-market conversion over 24 months—on par with NextEra or Clearway.

By tech, solar PV anchors with 2.8 GW added—65% of growth. Advanced 1.7 GW late-stage utility projects using N-type TOPCon bifacial modules and Nextracker trackers at 1.45:1 DC:AC ratios, targeting sub-$25 per MWh LCOEs in prime solar zones. Flagship: 1.2 GW Ironwood Solar expansion in Texas ERCOT, featuring agrivoltaics for sheep grazing, under 15-year hyperscaler PPA at blended $22 per MWh including 30% ITC plus 10% domestic content.

Wind added 850 MW onshore, focused U.S. Midwest and Australia. Key: 450 MW Prairie Winds III repower in Oklahoma swapping legacy turbines for Vestas V162-6.2 MW units, lifting capacity factors from 38% to over 50%. Models show post-tax IRRs above 12% at $30 per MWh conservative pricing under PTC evolution. In Australia, early works on 400 MW New South Wales via Clean Energy Finance Corporation amid AEMO's 82% renewables by 2030 forecast.

BESS grew fastest at 550 MW/1,100 MWh, addressing grid needs as renewables ramp. Standardized on Tesla Megapack 2XL for 95%+ roundtrip efficiency and four-hour dispatch. Addition: 300 MW/600 MWh co-located at Desert Sun solar in California, permitted under CPUC NEM 3.0 for standalone 30-50% ITC eligibility and SGIP-backed arbitrage of $150-250 per kW-month.

Green hydrogen: 50 MW electrolyzer via Plug Power JV for U.S. Gulf Coast industrial offtake, modeling under $2 per kg with cheap renewables and DOE Section 45V—early as electrolyzer capex falls 20% YoY per IRENA.

On milestones, Q2 emphasized delivery: COD on 650 MW across three projects added $185 million contracted revenue at 14-year average tenor. Includes full 300 MW Horizon Wind in Illinois, energizing under corporate PPA with Microsoft—our eighth hyperscaler this year per RE100's 25 GW demand.

NTP issued on 1.1 GW with Bechtel EPC underway, covering Arizona's Sun Valley BESS (200 MW/800 MWh) via $120 million tax equity flip at 8.5% IRR. Permitting advanced 2.3 GW to shovel-ready, zero NEPA holds via in-house team and FERC streamlining.

Geographically: North America 72% or 20.6 GW, boosted by IRA and queue fixes like California 2023 reforms and MISO Cycle 2022. Europe 15% or 4.3 GW, with UK North Sea Hybrid (offshore wind + floating solar) at £44 per MWh CfD. APAC 13% or 3.8 GW, accelerated 30% in Rajasthan solar by India's PLI.

We're emphasizing hybrid-plus-storage at 40% of new adds for CAISO/ERCOT ancillary premiums, adding 200-300 basis points to EBITDA margins. Supply chain: 85% U.S. content on solar BoP via First Solar thin-film, sidestepping Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act issues.

Ahead: 3-5 GW H2 adds, 2 GW FID by year-end, converting $2.2 billion investment pipeline. This focus on sub-$30 per MWh LCOEs, bankable offtake, and tech flexibility de-risks while sustaining 15-18% ROIC.

We expect to bring several new projects online soon, plus acquisitions and partnerships to expand.

Next, Emma will update on sustainability.

Emma Patel:
Thank you, Jordan. Sustainability is at the core of our business, and we are committed to reducing our environmental footprint and contributing to a cleaner, more sustainable future. In Q2, we cut Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 22% year-over-year through optimized turbine operations and 95% renewable-powered facilities, aligning with SBTi 1.5°C pathways. Energy efficiency gains hit 18% via AI predictive maintenance on our 12 GW fleet, saving 150 GWh annually.

Resource stewardship shines in agrivoltaics—like Ironwood Solar's sheep grazing dual-use—and water recycling at 85% in BESS sites, exceeding EPA benchmarks. Community efforts include $15 million in local grants for Midwest wind host training and California solar workforce programs, fostering 2,500 jobs.

Our ESG reporting earned MSCI AA rating, with biodiversity net gain on 80% projects via Verra-verified credits. These steps, tied to IRA bonuses and EU CBAM, deliver stakeholder value: lower WACC via green bonds and premium hyperscaler PPAs rewarding verified abatement. We're shaping a net-zero grid.

I'll now turn the call back to Mark for closing remarks.

Mark Thompson:
Thank you, Emma. Before Q&A, let me outline our strategic priorities and outlook for Q4 and FY 2025. Verdant—wait, Solara Renewables stays focused on the energy transition via our platform in utility solar PV, onshore/offshore wind, BESS, and green hydrogen. With clean energy at 12-15% CAGR to 2030 on falling LCOEs and policies like IRA, REPowerEU, and India PLI, we're primed for market share.

Backed by $4.2 billion backlog up 35% YoY and $12 billion-plus pipeline, our top three priorities:

First, ramp capacity and execution. Q4 CODs: 1.2 GW solar PV, 800 MW wind in U.S./Europe—including Arizona's 450 MW Desert Bloom Solar with $150 million IRA credits for 12%+ IRR at $28 per MWh PPAs. FY25 targets 4.5 GW adds—60% solar, 25% wind, 15% BESS—to exceed 15 GW operating.

U.S. drives 70% backlog; IRA-fueled 10-15% PPA escalations in ERCOT/PJM from datacenter hyperscalers Google/Microsoft. Advancing 1 GW solar-storage hybrids with 23.5% TOPCon and CATL LFP four-hour packs. Europe counters grid issues with 600 MW onshore in Germany/Poland on €200 billion REPowerEU; 300 MW Baltic Breeze offshore Q2 2025 with Siemens Gamesa 15 MW turbines at 55% capacity factor.

Supply secured: 85% 2025 polysilicon at $8-9 per kg from LONGi/Tongwei despite 20% YTD drops.

Second, tech innovation—$250 million R&D or 8% of revenues. Perovskite tandems at California pilot hit 28% lab efficiency, commercial 26% mid-2025 slashing LCOE under $20 per MWh; Oxford PV partnership for 500 MW FY26. LDES: 100 MWh Form Energy iron-air in Texas hybrids for 100-hour dispatch, $50 per MWh ERCOT PBR ancillaries solving duck curve. Green H2: Rotterdam 50 MW PEM ITM Power Q1 2025 commissioning, 5,000 tons yearly to Air Products; EU Hydrogen Bank bids for 200 MW more at $2.5 per kg by 2026 on 30% capex drop.

NVIDIA AI digital twins lift EPC margins 200 basis points via O&M foresight.

Third, optimize portfolio with discipline. FY25 EBITDA margins to 28-30% plus 300 basis points on 15% BOS cuts and Australia merchant via 20-year Rio Tinto CPPA at A$75 per MWh under NEM. New awards yield over 10%, shifting to 40% merchant/firm.

M&A: $450 million Horizon Wind 700 MW Midwest buy last month, accretive at 8 times EV/EBITDA. Eyeing Brazil solar auctions for low-curtailment, 50% cheaper land.

Outlook: Q4 revenue $850-900 million up 22% YoY, EBITDA $280-300 million at 32% margins, FCF $150 million post $200 million capex. FY25 $3.8-4.0 billion revenue—28% CAGR from FY23—EBITDA $1.1-1.2 billion.

Rates at 4-5% hedged 70% fixed with 2.8 times net debt/EBITDA buffer; Section 45X from Ohio 2 GW fab adds $100 million yearly.

Electrification (500 TWh U.S. EV demand by 2030), $50 billion YTD corporate PPAs per LevelTen, and 18-month 80% FY25 EBITDA visibility promise 20-25% TSR.

In conclusion, we are very pleased with our performance this quarter. We are confident that our strategic initiatives and our commitment to innovation and sustainability will drive continued growth and success in the years to come.

Operator, let's proceed with the Q&A session.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to register a question, please press star one on your telephone keypad. We will pause for a moment to compile the Q&A roster... Thank you. Our first question comes from John Smith with Green Energy Capital. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Can you discuss the impact of supply chain constraints on your project timelines?

Jordan Lee:
Thanks for the question, John. Supply chain pressures remain, but we've built resilience into our model. For instance, 85% of our solar balance-of-system uses U.S. content through First Solar thin-film partnerships, fully dodging Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act risks. We've locked long-term polysilicon at $8-9 per kg with LONGi and Tongwei, buffering 20% YTD price swings and Red Sea disruptions via Texas nacelle assembly for wind.

BESS sticks to Tesla Megapacks with high in-stock availability, and EPC with Bechtel keeps NTP-to-COD at under 18 months. Queue reforms in California and MISO have de-risked 60% of U.S. pipeline, with zero NEPA delays. This keeps our 85% historic conversion on track, with 2 GW FID-bound by year-end despite volatility. No major timeline slips expected.

Operator:
Thank you. Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Sustainable Investments Group. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
What is your strategy for expanding into emerging markets?

Mark Thompson:
Great question, Lisa. Emerging markets like APAC represent 13 to 15% of our pipeline at 3.8 GW, and we're accelerating selectively. In India, PLI incentives sped Rajasthan solar by 30%, including our 500 MW with Adani Green testing perovskite tandems for 25%+ efficiency. Australia's 400 MW New South Wales taps CEFC financing and AEMO's 82% renewables path, with NEM merchant upside like A$75 per MWh Rio Tinto CPPAs and Sun Cable extensions integrating H2.

We're eyeing Latin America, particularly Brazil auctions for low-curtailment solar at half U.S. land costs. Strategy: Tech-agnostic hybrids for grid stability, local JVs for permitting (e.g., Plug Power H2 Gulf Coast), and merchant hedges at $35 floors. IRA-like local incentives and hyperscaler demand make these 12%+ IRR plays, targeting 20% portfolio share by 2027 without diluting ROIC.

Operator:
Thank you. Our next question comes from David Rodriguez with EcoVentures. Please go ahead.

David Rodriguez:
How are you managing the increasing competition in the renewable energy sector?

Mark Thompson:
David, competition is heating up, but our edge is execution and differentiation. We're top-quartile with 28.7 GW pipeline and 85% conversion over 24 months, matching NextEra/Clearway while focusing sub-$30 per MWh LCOEs via TOPCon, Vestas repowers, and Tesla BESS. 40% hybrid-storage captures ancillary premiums adding 200-300 basis points.

Tech moat via perovskite pilots (28% lab), iron-air LDES, and AI twins boosts margins. Policy capture—IRA transfers $4.5 billion Q2, REPowerEU—plus 95% contracted backlog de-risks. M&A like Horizon 700 MW at 8x EV/EBITDA accretes immediately. Fortress balance sheet at 3.2 times leverage funds growth without dilution, sustaining 15-18% ROIC and 14.2% TTM. We're not just competing—we're leading through innovation and discipline.

Operator:
Thank you. At this time, there appear to be no further questions. I will now turn the call back over to Mark Thompson for any closing remarks.

Mark Thompson:
Thank you all for your participation in today's call. We appreciate your continued support of Solara Renewables. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
